title: Dynamic embeddings credit roll-forward + rerank spot-tier experiment
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Summary:
Run an experiment to validate a hybrid pricing construct for embeddings and reranking: (1) a per-vector baseline price that floors revenue + cost for low-volume consumers, (2) a dynamic batch discount engine that issues roll-forward credits for unused batch capacity (credit roll-forward), and (3) a rerank spot-tier priced for low-latency, high-priority traffic. The goal is to improve revenue predictability for Redwood while offering customers unit economics that scale with batch utilization.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Offering roll-forward credits for committed batch slots increases stickiness for mid-tier customers and increases monthly committed spend by >= 8% in pilot cohort.
- H2: A separate rerank spot-tier (lower latency SLA, higher per-vector) will capture >10% of existing rerank traffic with at least 12% uplift in ARPU for customers using rerank-heavy workflows.
- H3: A noise-floor on per-vector pricing (minimum per-request charge) prevents revenue leakage from tiny low-batch calls while keeping enterprises that batch at scale advantaged.

Success metrics (primary):
- Delta in monthly committed revenue from pilot customers (target +8% relative to baseline).
- Average effective per-vector price across cohort (target +5% blended uplift).
- Batch utilization increase (percent of vectors batched into multi-vector requests) target +12 percentage points.
- Churn signal: zero customers canceling because of pricing change within 30 days.

Design / experiment plan:
- Offer to 12 pilot customers (mix of AI-native startups and 2 enterprise accounts) a 3-month pilot with: 100k committed batch slots (example) + roll-forward credits up to 50% of unused slots; exposed as a billing line item "Batch Rollforward Credit".
- Implement rerank spot-tier toggle in Redwood Console and API with documented latency targets and per-vector surcharge.
- Add a noise-floor of $0.00002 per vector for requests < 16 vectors.
- Run two randomized cells: Control (status quo pricing) and Experiment (new hybrid pricing).
- Observe for 8 weeks post-enrollment, then evaluate 30/60/90 day revenue and usage.

Telemetry & tracking (analytics):
- Events: billing.commitment_purchased, billing.rollforward_credit_issued, api.request_batch_size, api.request_model_variant, billing.effective_per_vector_price, account.churn_intent.
- Dashboards: cohort revenue over time, batch-utilization heatmap, rerank-tier adoption chart. Links: https://dash.redwood.internal/embeddings-pricing-experiments (placeholder).

Implementation notes for Eng:
- Billing: add a new lineitem type "rollforward_credit" and an invoice flag to ensure credits apply automatically to future usage. Billing schema change required: bill_items.type enum -> add "rollforward_credit".
- API: add parameter in create_request: "billing_preference": "default|rerank_spot|dedicated_batch_slot".
- Console: new UI card for "Batch Commitment" showing available slots, used slots, and roll-forward forecast.

Legal / QSA / Contract implications:
- Need contract amendment template to allow credits to auto-apply and to define unused credit expiry (suggest 12 months).
- Update enterprise security questionnaire to include billing transparency and data residency implications of billing endpoints. QSA items to prepare: audit trail for credit issuance, invoice lineitem history, access controls for billing exports.
- Flag: Finance needs to confirm revenue recognition approach for roll-forward credits.

Risks & mitigations:
- Revenue leakage if roll-forward credits are too generous -> mitigation: cap roll-forward at 50% and run simulated revenue impact before rollout.
- Engineering complexity in billing -> mitigation: prototype as invoice-level adjustments without changing tokenized billing until validated.
- Customer confusion -> mitigation: clear UI/contract language, early customer success onboarding sessions.

Rollout / gating:
- Gate 1: Legal sign-off on contract language and expiry behavior.
- Gate 2: Billing integration tested in staging with synthetic invoices.
- Gate 3: Pilot launch to 12 customers.
- Gate 4: Evaluate 8-week data against success metrics; product committee decides expansion.
